tagline: The highest-volume tourism coast in the Caribbean — congested ferries crying out for a faster premium tier.
summary: Cancún and the Riviera Maya form the busiest tourism coast in the wider Caribbean, with Isla Mujeres, Cozumel and the Holbox/Tulum corridor drawing tens of millions of visitors. The Playa del Carmen↔Cozumel and Cancún↔Isla Mujeres ferries are heavily congested, and Cozumel is a top global cruise and dive port. This is a high-volume tourism + public-transit node where a premium, faster, quieter tier sits on top of enormous existing ferry demand.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Pioneer II owns the entire corridor: Cancún↔Isla Mujeres (~8 nm), Playa↔Cozumel (~12 nm), and the coastal runs to Tulum (~55 nm) and Holbox (~45 nm) — all inside all-electric range.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR (H2 2026+) is optional here — relevant for longer Yucatán/Caribbean reaches (e.g., toward Belize/Cozumel-to-Bahamas); the core network is Pioneer II.

competitive_landscape: Ultramar and Winjet run the dominant, heavily-used ferries; cruise tenders and dive boats fill the rest — overwhelming demand proof. The pain is congestion, queues, and Highway 307 traffic on the land alternative. There is no foiling incumbent.
seasonality: Atlantic hurricane season (Jun–Nov) is the constraint, with sargassum influxes (Apr–Aug) an added coastal nuisance; winter–spring is peak. The Cancún↔Isla Mujeres and Playa↔Cozumel channels are short and relatively protected.
regulatory_note: Mexican jurisdiction: API Quintana Roo, the Capitanía de Puerto (SEMAR), and FONATUR for tourism development. Clean-fleet operation aligns with the Mesoamerican Reef's protected status off Cozumel.
